name: Runner Extras - Document Service Session Seed
brief: Regression for issue #2487: NavSession.DocumentStorageService is never assigned, so every Document Service Management call NREs.
description: Base App codeunit 9510 "Document Service Management".SetServiceType calls the DotNet NavDocumentServiceHelper.SetDocumentServiceType, which forwards to Ncl.dll's DocumentServiceManagement.SetDocumentServiceType(session, type) -> session.DocumentStorageService.SetDocumentServiceType(type). On the runner's skeleton NavSession that property was never assigned, so it NREd on first touch: 19 of 25 tests in Microsoft's own Tests-SINGLESERVER bucket, codeunit 139101 "Document Service Mgmt Test", failed on this one throw before ever reaching the AL business logic under test. The fix seeds NavSession.DocumentStorageService with a real Ncl.dll NavDocumentStorageService instance at session bring-up, mirroring what BC's own DocumentServiceManagement.Reset(session) already does lazily -- not a substitute, the same concrete class real BC uses. This suite pins the runner-internal claim only: SetServiceType/GetServiceType round-trip without NRE-ing, and touching the surface that genuinely needs a document-service handler (not shipped in the platform artifacts the runner provisions) fails with BC's own named, diagnosed exception -- never a bare NullReferenceException. The plain BC-behaviour claims underneath (SetServiceType/GetServiceType semantics, TestConnection/SaveFile/IsServiceUri error text) are Microsoft's own codeunit 9510 and 139101, not owned by this repo or the al-language corpus, so they are not duplicated upstream here. Target is OnPrem, not Cloud: codeunit 9510 "Document Service Management" and its SetServiceType / TestConnection methods are declared Scope = OnPrem by Microsoft, so an AL object calling them cannot compile for Cloud (AL0296). The manifest said Cloud until issue #2725 made the runner honour app.json's target -- before that BcCompiler hard-coded CompilationTarget.OnPrem on both compile paths and the field was inert, so the wrong value cost nothing and nothing caught it.
